shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures set a five-week low on Friday amid diplomatic efforts to ease disruptions to Black Sea grain exports, analysts said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures set a five-week low on Friday amid diplomatic efforts to ease disruptions to Black Sea grain exports, analysts said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that India, Turkey, Egypt and other Middle Eastern countries were taking part in talks on unblocking shipping in the Black Sea.
Turkey submitted proposals to Moscow on the security of shipping in the Black Sea, but there were no substantive negotiations under way, Russian news agency Interfax reported.

and Ukraine result in a ceasefire, a Reuters analysis of industry data showed.

Wheat futures also came under pressure from early losses in CBOT corn and soybeans after a US-China summit failed to immediately deliver concrete announcements on additional Chinese agricultural purchases, an analyst said.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed down 3-3/4 cents at $7.03-1/4 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last down 5 cents at $7.62 a bushel, and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was 7 cents weaker at $7.13-1/2 a bushel.
